newsitem.title: FRANCE: European parliament chief cancels French talks.
newsitem.headline: European parliament chief cancels French talks.

text.p: The president of the European Parliament cancelled a meeting with French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette on Wednesday in protest at his harsh criticism of the assembly, a European Parliament spokesman said.

Jose-Maria Gil-Robles, who was on an inaugural visit to France, had demanded a clarification after de Charette branded the Strasbourg-based parliament "not worthy of the name" for criticising a French immigration bill.

The new conservative Spanish president called the minister's comment "an unacceptable judgement on the European Parliament, its role and its dignity" and said he hoped the terms used had gone beyond his thoughts.

But an unrepentant de Charette told the National Assembly at question time that the European Parliament had overstepped its powers by calling on the French government to withdraw a controversial bill to clamp down on illegal immigration.

"It is particularly shocking to see the European Parliament meddling in the national legislative process," he said, blaming France's opposition Socialists for proposing the motion narrowly adopted in Strasbourg last Thursday.

"Naturally, we have, and I am sure you have, the greatest respect for the European Parliament," he said to jeers from his centre-right coalition. "But if it wants to play an important role in future, it will have to respect national sovereignty."
